newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus says court rejects bid to block merger.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus says court rejects bid to block merger.

text.p: A French appeals court has rejected a bid by TF1 network, a subsidiary of French building company Bouygues, to block Canal Plus's merger with Nethold, Canal Plus said on Wednesday.

"This is a double victory for Canal Plus," the company said in a statement. "Last November 19, the Tribunal de Commerce dismissed TF1's request and ordered the firm to pay Canal Plus 100,000 francs. Today it was the appeals court's turn to throw out TF1's demands, fining it a further 100,000 francs and the cost of the appeal."

TF1 went to court on October 21 to demand either a suspension of the merger or the exclusion of all Nethold sports channels from the merger, citing a prior agreement between TF1 and Canal Plus on Eurosport in which Canal Plus had pledged not to compete with the sports channel.

Canal Plus had responded at the time that the merger did not jeopardise the interests of Eurosport, in which it was 33 percent shareholder. ESPN, a sports cable network that is part of The Walt Disney Co's ABC Inc subsidiary, is also a shareholder.
Nethold is jointly held by the South African-controlled industrial group Richemont and MCL-Multi Choice Ltd.
